claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children are you enquiring about for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm enquiring about my child, Alex. He's 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're enquiring about one child, Alex, who is 9 years old.

To help me assess your eligibility, I need to understand a bit more about your circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for letting me know. Before I can make a final determination, I need to check the specific eligibility rules regarding where you live. Let me read the official guidance on this.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for checking the guidance. I can see that you normally need to live in the UK to qualify for Child Benefit, but there are some exceptions for people living abroad.

**Can you tell me what country you're currently living in?** This will help me determine whether you might qualify under the special circumstances for living abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently living in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on the guidance I've reviewed, the rules state that you normally need to live in the UK to qualify for Child Benefit, but there are some exceptions for people living in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant.

I need to ask a few more questions to understand your full circumstances:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to check the specific rules about British citizens living abroad, as the guidance mentioned that you may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries.

Let me review the detailed eligibility criteria to see if Spain is one of those countries and what other conditions might apply.

**Can you tell me - are you working in Spain, or what is your current employment or financial situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm working in Spain, yes. I have a job there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. I need to understand a bit more about your work situation to properly assess your eligibility.

**Are you paying National Insurance contributions in the UK, or are you paying social security contributions in Spain as part of your employment there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm paying social security contributions in Spain as part of my employment there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Before I make a final determination, I need to check the detailed rules about living abroad more carefully, as there are specific provisions that apply to British citizens working in other countries.

Let me review the official guidance on this:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see from the guidance that there's mention of being able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in "certain countries," but the specific countries aren't listed on this main eligibility page. I also note that the rules mention Crown servants specifically.

**One more clarifying question: Does Alex live with you in Spain, or does Alex live in the UK with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me. He lives in the UK with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that important clarification. That changes things significantly. Let me check the specific rules about when a child lives with someone else, as this affects eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This is very helpful. I can see that if your child lives with someone else, you can still potentially get Child Benefit under certain conditions. Let me ask you a couple more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Are you currently making financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as towards his food, clothes, pocket money, or housing costs) while he lives with his mum in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I contribute towards his upkeep - things like clothes, pocket money, and helping with his costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's a key factor. Now I have one more important question:

**Is Alex's mum currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or do you know if anyone else is claiming it for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, his mum is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility. Let me review the rules carefully:

According to the guidance I've reviewed:

1. You live abroad (in Spain), not in the UK
2. Alex lives with his mum in the UK, not with you
3. Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him
4. Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child

The key rule states: "Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child." Since Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, you would not be eligible to claim it, as duplicate claims cannot be made for the same child.

Additionally, even though you do contribute to Alex's upkeep, the rules about continuing payments when a child lives with someone else apply when "nobody else claims." Since his mum is already claiming, this provision does not apply.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

Unfortunately, **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

The main reason is that only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child under UK law, and Alex's mum is already claiming it for him. Since she is the current recipient, you cannot make a duplicate claim.

**However**, if circumstances were to change – for example, if Alex's mum were no longer able to claim – you could potentially become eligible based on your financial contributions to his upkeep. If you'd like to discuss changing who claims Child Benefit for Alex, you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office directly to arrange this with his mum's agreement.

Since she is already the recipient, you cannot make a duplicate claim for the same child. While you do contribute to Alex's upkeep, the rules that allow continued payments beyond 8 weeks when a child lives with someone else specifically state this applies 'if nobody else claims' - which is not your situation.

Under UK law, only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any given time. Although you contribute financially to Alex's upkeep, this does not override the fundamental rule that duplicate claims cannot exist for the same child. If you wished to claim instead of his mum, you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to arrange a change of claimant, but this would be a decision between you and Alex's mum rather than a separate claim for both of you."
